First mission to the Jupiter Trojans — primordial asteroids co-orbiting Jupiter at the L4 and L5 Lagrange points, believed to preserve material from the outer protoplanetary disc. First asteroid flyby: Dinkinesh (2023-11-01), at which the contact-binary satellite Selam was discovered. Bonus main-belt asteroid Donaldjohanson flyby 2025-04. Eurybates encounter 2027-08; Patroclus-Menoetius binary 2033-03 closes the primary mission.

Cape Canaveral SLC-41, 2021-10-16. Lucy is the first mission to study the Jupiter Trojans — primordial asteroids leading and trailing Jupiter at its L4 and L5 Lagrange points by 60°. The trojans are believed to be remnants of the outer protoplanetary disc, captured into the Lagrange points during early solar system migration. Lucy's 12-year primary mission visits eight asteroids on separate solar orbits — two main-belt (Dinkinesh, Donaldjohanson) and six Trojans, plus their satellites — a record for a single planetary science mission.
Centaur upper stage delivers Lucy onto a complex multi-encounter trajectory using three Earth gravity assists (2022, 2024, 2030) to reach both Trojan swarms.
2022-10-16. First EGA accelerates Lucy onto a higher heliocentric orbit, reaching beyond Mars.

2023-11-01. Closest approach to 152830 Dinkinesh (~790 m main-belt asteroid). Lucy's first-ever asteroid encounter. Imaging revealed the contact-binary satellite Selam — a previously unknown moon — a headline discovery independent of the primary Trojan mission.

2025-04-20. Closest approach 960 km at 13.4 km/s past asteroid 52246 Donaldjohanson — a main-belt contact-binary asteroid about 8 km long, named for the discoverer of the Lucy hominid fossil. Bonus target added late in mission design to test instruments before the Trojan encounters.
2027-08-12. Lucy arrives at the L4 Trojan cloud.

Closest approach within 1,000 km at 5.8 km/s (2027-08-11) past 3548 Eurybates, the largest member of the L4 Eurybates family — a 64-km C-type fragment of a larger parent body. Queta is Eurybates's 1-km moon, discovered by Hubble in 2018. Lucy's first Trojan encounter.
2027-09-15. 21-km P-type Trojan; the Lucy team found a satellite during a stellar occultation in March 2022; it doesn't yet have a name.
2030-12-26. Final EGA accelerates Lucy outbound to the trailing L5 cloud.

2033-03-02. The mission climax: encounter with binary Trojan Patroclus-Menoetius. Patroclus (113 km) + Menoetius (104 km) are a nearly-equal-mass binary on the L5 side — the largest Trojan binary known. Closest approach 1,000 km at 8.4 km/s. After 12 years of cruise, Lucy will have visited 11 bodies across 8 asteroids and their satellites — a record number of objects on separate heliocentric orbits for any planetary science mission.
First mission to the Jupiter Trojans; visits 11 bodies across 8 asteroids and their satellites in a single 12-year trajectory — a record number of objects on separate solar orbits

Lucy reaches for the L4 and L5 Lagrange clouds — populations of primordial asteroids leading and trailing Jupiter by 60°, believed to preserve material from the outer protoplanetary disc. Three Earth gravity assists (2022, 2024, 2030) shape a single trajectory that visits seven Trojan asteroids plus bonus main-belt targets. First asteroid encounter: 152830 Dinkinesh (2023-11-01, ~790 m), at which imaging revealed the contact-binary satellite Selam. Bonus main-belt: Donaldjohanson 2025-04. L4 swarm: Eurybates + moon Queta (2027-08), Polymele (2027-09), Leucus (2028-04), Orus (2028-11). After EGA-3 (2030-12), the trailing L5 swarm: Patroclus-Menoetius binary (2033-03) — the largest Trojan binary known, a fitting climax for the mission's namesake (Lucy the hominid fossil; Patroclus-Menoetius the two characters that fell together in the Iliad).
Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral SLC-41.
2023-11-01. First asteroid flyby — ~790 m main-belt body; satellite Selam (contact binary) discovered.
Main-belt bonus flyby 2025-04. C-type contact-binary asteroid about 8 km long.
Final Earth assist 2030-12. Heads to L5 cloud.
